svg.title: The East India Company & Mughal Bengal (1600–1765)
svg.desc: KS3 Year 8 historical GIS atlas map of the undivided Mughal Indian Subcontinent and zoomed Bengal & Ganges Delta inset (1600–1765), showing Mughal capitals Delhi and Agra, East India Company fortified coastal factories at Surat (1612), Madras (1639), Bombay (1668), and Calcutta (1690), Robert Clive and Mir Jafar at the Battle of Plassey (1757), Buxar (1764), and the 1765 Treaty of Allahabad granting the Bengal Diwani.

Clive bribes Mir Jafar; Nawab falls

g.text: KEY • FROM TRADING COMPANY TO BENGAL RULER

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 8 ENQUIRY: THE FIRST BRITISH EMPIRE (1600–1783)
The East India Company & Mughal Bengal (1600–1765)
Chartered in 1600 to trade spices & cotton, the East India Company built sepoy-guarded coastal factories across Mughal India.
After bribing Mir Jafar at Plassey (1757) and winning the 1765 Diwani, a private London company taxed 20 million people in Bengal.
